answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit bids, and slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud or duplicate control. This raises the cost of Sybils: an attacker must fund each identity separately, keep capital tied up, and risk losing it. A harbor reputation can grow like a vine only through verified work; timber-like collateral makes multiplying identities expensive, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker outright.
